hypotheses.name: Signed paired-throw basement-gravity concordance under low-relief alluvial cover
hypotheses.signature: Test antisymmetric flank profiles across +/-400 m strike-oriented corridors: a positive hanging-wall step in depth_to_base_surf and a negative step in iso_grav_anom must share the same downthrown polarity along >=900 m strike continuity, weighted higher where det_elev scarp relief is muted by basin fill, and compared against a polarity-scrambled control at identical 300 m submodular emission budget.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: USGS/INGENIOUS Quaternary fault mapping captures subaerial range-front scarps where det_elev steps are sharp, but systematically under-maps intrabasin blind growth faults and buried accommodation steps beneath Holocene playa/alluvial cover where sedimentation erases surface scarps while cumulative dip-slip preserves concordant basement-depth and gravity steps.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: All executed GEMSDOE86 lanes (GMC, RMRB, WVB, GFCO, KSLB, CTHB) rely on unsigned gradient magnitudes, tilt zero-crossings, or Blakely curvature ridges and discard cross-flank dip-slip polarity concordance; PR #60 mentioned signed paired-throw in prose without ever loading training_features.tif or implementing it (IR-86-SPT-02).
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted pre-Tertiary erosional paleovalley margins or buried caldera moat walls infilled by low-density tuffaceous basin sediments; inversion artifacts.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Highest qualitative priority among local-feature candidates: directly targets intrabasin blind dip-slip faults at low CPU cost (~35 min once protocol gate permits). No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low-medium: oriented +/-400 m antisymmetric flank filters, polarity-scrambled control, and existing 300 m submodular decoder.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: raw competition layers have pinned mirrors, but execution remains blocked by protocol_preflight.require_feasible() under the literal 17GEMSDOE dense-witness rule.

hypotheses.name: Cross-corridor GeoDAWN magnetic marker-horizon phase-correlation offset
hypotheses.signature: For label-free candidate line orientations, phase-correlate transverse magnetic marker ridges on opposite +/-700 m flanks. Require a consistent nonzero lateral translation across adjacent strike windows and a weaker zero-shift match, retaining both dextral and sinistral slip senses.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Accommodation-zone transfer faults and oblique Walker Lane / Humboldt relay structures cut buried Tertiary volcanic sheets across basin floors without building prominent range-front topographic scarps, leaving coherent lateral marker offsets where surface mapping is blank.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: GFCO compares TMI with upward-continued TMI; GMC computes cross-gradients between gravity and magnetics; WVB and CTHB use local-wavenumber, tilt-phase, and hydrothermal couplings. None estimate two-sided flank-to-flank lateral phase translation of transverse magnetic markers.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted intrusive contacts, primary Miocene lava-flow lobe terminations, GeoDAWN survey-block flight-line tie seams, and remanent magnetization reversals.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Second qualitative priority: physically orthogonal strike-slip / transfer-zone detector using local bands without external downloads. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: multi-azimuth split-window FFT phase correlation, seam controls, and buffered LOQO validation (~65 min CPU).
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: blocked prior to feature construction by protocol_preflight.require_feasible() under the pinned dense-witness overlap stop.

hypotheses.name: Magnetotelluric crustal conductance boundary x geodetic transtensional dilatancy bridge
layers: external USGS Great Basin MT electrical conductance grids (DOI 10.5066/P9TWT2LU)
external INGENIOUS GPS geodetic strain-rate & dilatation archive (DOE GDR 1391 geodetics, DOI 10.15121/1881483)
competition rtp_tilt_deriv (Band 14) and heat_flow / 2m temperature compilations (DOI 10.5066/P9BZPVUC)
hypotheses.signature: Co-align steep horizontal log10 electrical conductance gradients at 1-5 km depth with positive horizontal geodetic dilatation (eps_xx + eps_yy > 0) and maximum shear strain rate, sharpened onto 100 m corridors along GeoDAWN RTP magnetic tilt zero-crossings.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Blind hydrothermal fault conduits in the Humboldt structural zone and northern Walker Lane frequently lack Holocene surface scarps and modern catalog seismicity, yet hot saline fluids plus smectite-illite clay alteration produce strong subsurface MT conductance contrasts inside actively dilating crust — the core blind geothermal target emphasized by INGENIOUS Phase 2 expert relabeling.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: No GEMSDOE86 lane ingests either USGS MT electrical conductance (10.5066/P9TWT2LU) or INGENIOUS geodetic strain/dilatation tensors (GDR 1391 geodetics); H86D-CTHB used only gravity, magnetics, radiometrics, SGMC contacts, and shallow geothermometry.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Closed-basin evaporitic playa brines and stratiform Paleozoic graphitic/sulfidic black shales generating non-tectonic high conductance.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Third qualitative priority: strong physical complementarity for blind geothermal conduits, gated behind external archive mirroring and coarse-to-100 m downscaling verification. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: external ScienceBase/GDR archive pinning, EPSG:32611 reprojection, leakage-canary check against Qfaults-derived layers, and buffered holdout testing.
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: USGS ScienceBase MT electrical conductance release (https://doi.org/10.5066/P9TWT2LU) and DOE GDR Submission 1391 geodetics archive (https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391, CC-BY-4.0), excluding qfaults_ingenious shapefiles to prevent label leakage.
hypotheses.obtainability: Public metadata and CC-BY-4.0 archive listings on https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391 and https://gbcge.org/current-projects/ingenious/ were verified on 2026-10-24, but direct binary download from gdr.openei.org / sciencebase.gov is blocked inside this sandbox's outbound allowlist (GitHub/PyPI/npm only) until SHA-pinned into a permitted mirror.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: public CC-BY-4.0 releases exist, but raw MT conductance and geodetic grid bytes are not mirrored or hash-pinned in this workspace, and protocol_preflight.require_feasible() also blocks execution.

hypotheses.name: Watershed-crossing 1-m 3DEP LiDAR micro-scarp curvature persistence
layers: official USGS 3DEP bare-earth 1 m DEM tiles (competition 1m_DEM_links.csv)
hypotheses.signature: Measure signed 5-25 m cross-strike profile curvature steps on native 1 m bare-earth LiDAR DEMs that retain strike and downthrown polarity across independently delineated drainage divides, vetoing candidates aligned with steepest-descent channels, constant-elevation pluvial shorelines, or road embankments.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Low-slip (0.3-1.5 m) late Quaternary piedmont and intrabasin scarps are smoothed below noise in 30-100 m DEM products and missed in pre-LiDAR airphoto mapping, yet persist cleanly across multiple ephemeral fan catchments at 1 m LiDAR resolution.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Zero GEMSDOE86 lanes ingest native 1 m 3DEP LiDAR tiles; GFCO, WVB, and CTHB operated exclusively on 100 m pre-aggregated morphological layers without sub-pixel scarp dipole extraction or cross-divide persistence.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan wave-cut shoreline benches, fluvial terrace risers, and highway/railroad grades.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Fourth qualitative priority: high physical specificity on subtle piedmont scarps, ranked fourth due to multi-gigabyte external tile-processing cost. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: native 1 m DEM tile streaming, hydrologic catchment conditioning, and 100 m EPSG:32611 summary raster generation (~2-4 hr preprocessing).
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM GeoTIFFs indexed by the competition's 1m_DEM_links.csv (documented in https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/96647.pdf).
hypotheses.obtainability: Official competition rules (https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/96647.pdf, verified 2026-10-24) confirm 1 m USGS DEM features are part of the official public data package, but neither authenticated DrivenData 1m_DEM_links.csv nor USGS TNM tile hosts are reachable from this sandbox allowlist.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: native 1 m DEM tiles and coverage manifest are not present in this checkout, and protocol_preflight.require_feasible() blocks model execution.

required_validation_after_blockers_are_r: Assign one method lane; restore and hash-verify the actual shared cached feature stack and a current complete accessible registry.
Preserve the literal rho (>0.90) and 3-px dot-overlap (>0.70) limits; do not exempt the 17GEMSDOE dense continuous witness without an explicit owner-approved protocol revision.

Freeze buffered whole-component folds and fixed budgets before touching withheld labels; derive every catalogue feature strictly from fold-visible faults outside the buffer (never mask full existing_faults.tif as PR #60 did).
Run single-feature and combined leakage canaries before trusting any holdout number; max(AUC, 1-AUC) > 0.90 stops the run, and AUC <= 0.52 flags a non-informative feature.

Use the pinned shared evaluate_holdout.py and submission_writer.py unchanged; report pooled HOLDOUT-DTI with evaluator version, withheld-positive pixel count, physical-block 95% CI, and paired delta vs H86D-CTHB and fold-fair R0.
At most 3 experiments or 2 hours per session; negative results are first-class deliverables, and promotion to a DrivenData weekly submission slot remains a separate selector step.
